Lessons.Title: Comparing Quadratic and Exponential Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: compare quadratic growth with exponential growth, using tables, graphs, successive ratios and reasoned long-run comparisons; discover that an increasing exponential eventually overtakes a fixed-degree polynomial. Original Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U06:L04 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/6/4/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/6/4/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source specifically compares growing square tiles with doubling tiles.

Original functions for integer step n≥0: Q(n)=n² tiles and E(n)=2^n tiles. Values n0 through6: Q0,1,4,9,16,25,36; E1,2,4,8,16,32,64. At n3 quadratic9>exponential8; at n4 both16; at n5 exponential32>quadratic25. Looking only at a short range could yield an incorrect prediction about long-run dominance.

Quadratic successive output ratios are not constant: Q2/Q1=4, Q3/Q2=9/4, Q4/Q3=16/9. Exponential ratio E(n+1)/E(n)=2 for all n. A graph should use common scales and show the later crossing rather than imply it is an exponential's fixed increase.

Student task: graph both for n0–7, justify each crossing/ordering change, compare the first and second differences of Q with exponential ratios, and discuss the mathematical distinction between eventual growth and a real-world material limit. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for correct tables, comparison at shared inputs, factor/rate explanation and carefully qualified conclusion.

KeyConcepts.Title: Quadratic growth
KeyConcepts.Definition: A fixed squared term gives nonconstant first differences and constant second differences for equal steps.

KeyConcepts.Title: Exponential growth
KeyConcepts.Definition: A fixed multiplier b>1 is applied each step.

KeyConcepts.Title: Crossover at shared input
KeyConcepts.Definition: One function may dominate in one interval, then another later.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming a quadratic is multiplied by a fixed factor each step
Inferring permanent dominance from a finite graph alone
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A limited window may hide crossing.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Inspect longer range and structural change.

SummaryPoints: Quadratic and exponential functions can exchange which is larger.
Q3 exceeds E3, while E5 exceeds Q5 in the chosen sample.
Quadratic first differences and exponential ratios behave differently.
Teacher reviews graphs and long-run reasoning.
